description: Covering the recent round of artificial intelligence apocalypse warnings, I’ve tried to reject this cult-like deference to all-powerful computer systems and the inevitability rhetoric: If Silicon Valley doesn’t build them first, someone else — likely China — will. Yet a recent spate of incidents in the US has spurred a fresh, heated debate over the safety of letting AI systems act on their own. A growing number of researchers inside the companies involved are also warning of “existential” danger

Eighteen years later, in July 2022, the 42-year-old Korean Canadian became the music director of the Ann Arbor Symphony Orchestra in Michigan. title: When this cellist's hand stopped working, he picked up a baton instead

description: Facing a projected shortage of nearly 1 million care workers in the coming decades, South Korea plans to use robots and artificial intelligence monitoring systems to help fill gaps in care for its aging population, the Ministry of Health and Welfare said Tuesday. Pilot programs will begin next year in more than 400 households in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, and Mokpo and Yeongam, South Jeolla Province, alongside trials of AI welfare consultations in 10 regions. title: Korea plans round-the-clock AI eldercare from 2028

description: Samsung Electronics is turning more to China’s BOE for TV panels, with purchases forecast to double this year as the Korean company reshuffles its LCD suppliers. The shift comes as BOE Chairman Chen Yanshun reportedly plans to visit Korea next week to meet Samsung Electronics CEO Roh Tae-moon. Neither company has announced the meeting, but local media reports citing industry sources said TV LCD supply and pricing are expected to be on the agenda. title: BOE chief set for Korea visit as Samsung boosts panel orders

description: Prosecution reform is exposing fault lines across the liberal camp as an unprecedented overhaul takes shape, splitting the camp over a cause that has united the bloc for decades. President Lee Jae Myung and the minor progressive Rebuilding Korea Party are locked in an unusually public confrontation over how far the overhaul should go, whether a career prosecutor should lead the new investigative agency and whether the reform can now be considered largely complete. title: Prosecution reform, once rallying cry, tests liberal unity

description: The Grammy Awards’ first best Asian pop music performance category will go ahead during the 2027 awards ceremony, but without two of the current biggest names in K-pop: BTS and Stray Kids. BTS announced in July that it would not submit music for consideration for the 2027 Grammy Awards, objecting to the newly created category and saying it hoped music could be appreciated without being divided by region or language. Stray Kids also made the choice to sit out this year’s submissions process. JYP
title: What will Grammys’ Asian pop category look like without BTS, Stray Kids?

According to Stefan Sagmeister, the answer depends on how far back you're willing to look. The New York-based Austrian designer is best known for creating album art and packaging for the Rolling Stones, Lou Reed and Talking Heads, work that has won him two Grammys. description: S-1 Corp. is a small part of Samsung’s sprawling business empire. But an activist investor’s bid for Samsung affiliates’ stakes in the security company poses the question: When should a conglomerate’s companies sell their holdings in one another? title: Why is an activist targeting Samsung’s stakes in S-1?

Eight of the National Assembly's 17 standing committees began their annual inspections of government agencies Tuesday, kicking off a three-week audit scheduled to run through Oct. 27. description: Foreign tourists’ card spending in Seoul rose nearly three times as fast as visitor numbers in the first eight months of the year, nearly matching the total spent throughout last year. Foreign tourists spent 7.78 trillion won ($5.79 billion) by card in the capital from January through August, up 59.9 percent from a year earlier, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday. That growth rate was about 2.8 times the 21.6 percent increase in visitors over the same period. The eight-month spending
title: Foreign tourist spending in Seoul jumps nearly 60%

description: The 31st edition of the Busan International Film Festival begins its 10-day run Tuesday, with the festival seeking to bolster its global presence with its first "A-list" accreditation by a prominent global organization of filmmakers. This year's event will run through Oct. 15 in the southeastern South Korean city of Busan with 247 official selections from 59 nations, which marks the biggest slate since 2019, according to organizers. Of the total, 95 films will have their world premieres at BIFF.
title: Busan film fest kicks off with 'A-list' status for 1st time

description: Seoul shares turned lower on profit-taking after opening higher Tuesday, as concerns over rising bond yields at multidecade highs weighed on investor sentiment. After opening 0.58 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index fell 8.14 points, or 0.12 percent, to 6,995.60 as of 9:15 a.m. Investors are now turning their attention to upcoming corporate earnings, although higher interest rates, elevated energy costs and renewed inflation worries are pushing up global bond yields.
title: Seoul stocks turn lower after opening higher on profit-taking

description: Yoon Ina moved up in the women's world golf rankings after finishing runner-up at the LPGA Tour's Lotte Championship. Yoon received an average of 3.52 points in the rankings released Monday, climbing six spots from No. 23 last week to No. 17. She finished second at the Lotte Championship, which ended Sunday, after a close battle for the title with Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand. title: Yoon Ina rises to No. 17 in world rankings

Kim will attempt to win the tournament for a third consecutive year when the $2 million event begins Thursday at New Korea Country Club in Goyang, Gyeonggi Province.
